#5237. Cardano’s Leios Scaling Work Advances, but November Update Signals No Mainnet Launch

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Cardano’s November 6 development report describes progress on the Leios scaling design, including endorser-block production, chain-selection checks and a new prototype. The work remains in development. It is not a mainnet deployment or proof that Cardano has already delivered the throughput improvements under discussion.

Blockchain scaling announcements can make incremental engineering sound like an overnight transformation. Cardano’s latest weekly report is more useful when read for what the teams actually changed: pieces of consensus code, prototype behaviour and supporting developer tools.

The November 6 Cardano development update says the consensus team advanced Leios on its main development branch, with work on endorser-block production, certificate checks during chain selection and relaying votes. The report explicitly identifies these as development activities rather than an upgrade already running on the public network.

Leios is intended to explore greater processing capacity without discarding the chain’s consensus and security assumptions. One challenge is getting participants to agree on which blocks and endorsements are valid while keeping the communication and computational burden manageable.

The weekly report says prototype release rc-2026w44 added adaptive endorsements. In the team’s description, the system can reduce endorser-block sizes when it receives insufficient votes, which could help the prototype behave more predictably under varying network conditions.

The previous prototype, rc-2026w43, had reduced a certifying-block forging operation from as much as 0.9 seconds to milliseconds. That is a measurement of an internal development task. It should not be presented as the time a user now needs to wait for confirmation on Cardano mainnet.

The report also mentions an update to the ouroboros-consensus library that lowers memory use when writing ledger snapshots. Such work is less dramatic than a headline throughput figure, but it is important if a network expects more participants to operate reliable nodes under heavier loads.

Leios is not Cardano’s only scaling effort. A separate Hydra team update, covering work from October 26 to November 1, described improvements to monitoring of snapshots, queues and persistence. Better dashboards and alert examples can help operators identify faults before they turn into service interruptions.

The same reporting period included fixes for certain error cases and continuing work on capacity and start-up behaviour. The development update did not announce a new Hydra release. That distinction matters to users deciding whether a capability is already available in deployed software.

The Plutus team, meanwhile, finalised cost models for several built-in operations and added 65 conformance cases for new Value built-ins. These are steps toward predictable smart-contract execution and easier developer testing, rather than an announcement that applications can suddenly execute at unlimited scale.

Scaling is also a theme beyond Cardano. NewsBTC has looked at Solana’s network and settlement infrastructure, another example of why technical progress needs to be separated from user-facing deployment claims.

A weekly engineering report is useful evidence that teams are working, but it is not by itself evidence of adoption, lower fees or guaranteed future performance. The harder questions involve external testing, network-wide coordination, adversarial conditions and how improvements behave at scale.

For developers, the next milestones include additional prototype measurements, compatibility updates and a credible path from research branches to broadly tested releases. For readers watching ADA, the distinction between experiment, software release and mainnet activation is particularly important.

The bottom line is that Cardano’s scaling programme has made documented technical progress. It has not crossed the finish line. Understanding that difference is more useful than turning every prototype result into a promise of instant transactions.

#5234. World Liberty Financial Proposes WLFI Buybacks as Governance Token Comes Under Pressure

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: World Liberty Financial announced a buyback programme for its WLFI governance token on November 5, with initial funding that may include income from reserves backing its USD1 stablecoin. The company says the plan is intended to support long-term governance participation, but a buyback does not guarantee a token price recovery or reveal how much money will ultimately be spent.

A cryptocurrency buyback sounds reassuring to holders: a project plans to purchase some of its own tokens rather than leave all buying to the market. But the details determine whether that policy creates meaningful change or simply produces another headline.

World Liberty Financial, the crypto venture associated with President Donald Trump and his family, has announced a programme to repurchase WLFI governance tokens. According to reporting on the November 5 announcement, the initiative could draw on revenue from reserves that back World Liberty’s USD1 stablecoin, alongside other sources of funding.

The company says the programme is meant to encourage sustained participation in governance and strengthen voting power among long-term token holders. It has described the arrangement as an ongoing part of its strategy rather than a one-off intervention.

There are important unanswered questions, however. The announcement as reported does not establish a fixed total budget, the precise timetable of purchases or the volume of tokens that will be bought in any particular period. Without those details, investors cannot reliably calculate the potential effect on the circulating supply or market liquidity.

A buyback is also not the same as a token burn. An issuer or affiliated entity might acquire tokens and hold them, distribute them later or subject them to separate governance rules. The effect depends on what happens after purchase and whether the tokens remain able to participate in votes or return to the market.

The reference to stablecoin reserve income warrants particular scrutiny. Reserve earnings, reserves themselves and funds belonging to token holders or users are not interchangeable concepts. The company will need to be clear about the funding pathway if the programme is to be judged on financial substance.

World Liberty Financial was co-founded with involvement from Trump family members and partners. Reuters reported that the family holds a substantial economic interest in the venture, creating an intersection between a politically prominent business and a market in which regulation remains a live issue.

Supporters of the project may view the buyback as an attempt to align incentives and support long-term governance. Critics may question conflicts of interest, disclosure and whether a token with a prominent political connection can be evaluated independently of public office and policy decisions. Both questions deserve examination without assuming that a buyback proves misconduct or that political backing guarantees commercial success.

These governance considerations also extend beyond World Liberty. NewsBTC has covered how custody, market structures and token settlement are changing as institutions enter crypto. A clear governance structure matters when investors are asked to hold tokens whose practical rights differ from ordinary company shares.

The most useful next disclosure would identify the buyback budget, purchases actually completed, average prices and the final treatment of acquired tokens. Regular public reporting would allow holders to compare promises with execution and distinguish token-market operations from the separate stablecoin business.

Price reactions should also be interpreted carefully. A token can rise or fall for reasons unrelated to a buyback, including broader crypto-market conditions and changes in liquidity. Purchases can help support demand at the margin, but they cannot make a token immune to selling or establish its fair value.

For now, World Liberty has announced a policy intention. Whether that intention changes WLFI’s supply dynamics, governance or investor confidence is something future disclosures—not the launch announcement alone—will have to establish.

#5232. Hollywood Studios Quietly Ban Staff From Betting on Prediction Markets: Report

Hollywood Studios Quietly Ban Staff From Betting on Prediction Markets: Report

Hollywood studios and production companies have been quietly issuing guidelines barring employees from betting on prediction markets, entertainment industry trade paper The Hollywood Reporter reported on Thursday.

The warnings prohibit staff from betting on events such as studio earnings, casting decisions and release dates, or passing information to friends and family so they can bet instead, according to the report. At least one company has reportedly set up a hotline for employees to anonymously report colleagues suspected of placing bets.

The Hollywood Reporter's own parent company, Penske Media, has also updated its employee handbook in recent weeks to ban bets on "award nominations, casting decisions, production timelines and release dates," the outlet said.

The rules extend long-standing bans on insider trading in the stock market to platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket, which let users bet on everything from who will be cast as the next James Bond to who will be voted off a reality show.

"You now have, essentially, an explosion in the number of employers who have to think about insider trading rules from an ethical standpoint," Joshua Mitts, a law professor at Columbia University who studies prediction markets, told the outlet.

Enforcing those rules may be another matter. "With blockchain-based trading, it can be basically impossible if you know how to use a mixer correctly and know how to hide your identity behind multiple layers of intermediation," Mitts said.

Some bookmakers are already spooked. Betting site BetOnline temporarily pulled its market on the next James Bond this week after a sudden wave of "sharp money" pushed actor Callum Turner above longtime favorite Jack Lowden, raising concerns about a leak, according to the report.

Entertainment insiders have been caught before. In February, Kalshi said a video editor at MrBeast's company had made about $5,000 using confidential information to bet on MrBeast content; he was fired and fined $20,000.

Federal prosecutors have also brought cases over insider trading on prediction markets. In April, an active-duty U.S. soldier was charged with using classified information about the raid to capture Nicolás Maduro to bet on Polymarket. In May, a Google engineer was charged with commodities fraud, wire fraud and money laundering over Polymarket bets allegedly placed using confidential company data. Both cases are pending.

Governments have moved too. California, New York and Illinois have banned state employees from using nonpublic information to bet on prediction markets, while the platforms have rolled out their own surveillance tools. Polymarket has investigated dozens of bets on the U.S. midterm elections.

One kind of entertainment bet is already off the table. Under the Onion Futures Act of 1958, U.S. law explicitly bans just two types of futures contracts: those on onions and those on movie box office receipts, The Hollywood Reporter noted.

Bitcoin snapped a seven-week holding above the 50-week moving average (MA) with a weekly close at $74,968. According to the latest Galaxy Research report, BTC settled 0.7% under this key line, which now sits at $75,488.

Alex Thorn, the firm’s head of research, calls it a fakeout. The history is on his side: it's standard Bitcoin mechanics to slip back under the 50-week MA right after a bear-market bottom, and it's what shapes the structure of the four-year cycle. It has happened exactly twice before.

Losing the trendline again right after reclaiming it is how the biggest cryptocurrency has always behaved. Previous cycles played out like this:

The current chart is running the same script. From the $123,524 peak in October 2025, the coin bled 51.8% into the June cycle bottom at $59,517. A rebound then shoved the price back above the 50-week MA at $81,195. Today’s price is 7.7% off that September reclaim level, yet Bitcoin maintains a comfortable 26% cushion above the June bottom.

Thorn isn’t selling certainty. Two cycles is a thin sample, and bottoms only get confirmed in the rearview mirror. The margin for error is wide: in 2012, Bitcoin broke down again from 18% above the line, while in 2015 it held from just 8% above.

“Bitcoin just closed below its 50 week moving average after holding above it for 7 consecutive weeks. Two other times (2011-12 & 2019-20) btc closed below its 50w after reclaiming its post-bear bottom. Neither of those times did the bear make a new lower low (weekly close data),” the analyst notes.

One level kills the bull case for this 4-year cycle: $59,517. Galaxy Research says on-chain metrics, whale positioning and market sentiment all point to a consolidation that is technically ripe for stacking on spot. The technical case stays alive as long as Bitcoin reclaims the 50-week MA and holds it within the next month.

#5225. S&P 500 Plunges, Wall Street Fears Circuit Breaker, Just One Day After Trump Celebrated Record Highs

S&P 500 Plunges, Wall Street Fears Circuit Breaker, Just One Day After Trump Celebrated Record Highs

President Donald Trump's celebration of Wall Street's highs aged rather poorly. Less than 24 hours after boasting about Americans' retirement accounts going "through the roof," the S&P 500 plunged as much as 3.8% Thursday, bringing emergency trading halts into the conversation.

The selloff prompted traders to monitor the market's circuit-breaker thresholds, which can temporarily shut down trading across U.S. stock exchanges when losses become too severe. The S&P 500 would need to fall another 3.2 percentage points from its decline to trigger the first emergency halt.

The timing is particularly awkward for Trump, who has repeatedly pointed to stock market performance as evidence of his administration's economic success.

"Stock Market just hit another Record High—91 Days in just a short period of time—Less than two years. Your 401(k)s are through the roof," Trump wrote Wednesday on his Truth Social account. He closed the message with "Record Setting All! President DONALD J. TRUMP."

Wall Street had rallied Wednesday following the Democratic Party's sweeping midterm election victories. The S&P 500 gained 1.6%, its strongest daily performance in three months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped more than 1,500 points to 53.361 points.

Thursday's losses erase that rally in a single session, with technology stocks taking the biggest beating.

The U.S. stock market has three emergency thresholds designed to slow panic selling. These mechanisms, known as circuit breakers, automatically suspend trading when the S&P 500 falls by a specified percentage from its previous closing price.

The first threshold is a 7% decline, corresponding to an S&P 500 level of 7,150.41 points for Thursday's session. Reaching that level before 3:25 p.m. ET would trigger a 15-minute halt across US equity markets.

The circuit breaker level is located in the following chart’s blue line

A 13% decline, or 6,689.09 points, would trigger another 15-minute suspension. The most severe threshold comes at 20%, or 6,150.89 points, which would shut down trading for the remainder of the day.

Under the New York Stock Exchange's rules, the first two circuit breakers stop applying at 3:25 p.m. ET, while the 20% threshold remains active throughout the session.

The rules apply to the entire U.S. equity market, not just stocks included in the S&P 500. A market-wide halt would also suspend trading in companies listed on the Nasdaq and other US exchanges.

The technology sector was particularly hard hit as investors continued digesting the consequences of Tuesday's election results. At around 11 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite had fallen nearly 5%, while the S&P 500 was down 3.2%.

Nvidia lost more than 6%, while the broader semiconductor index plunged nearly 11%. Companies involved in building AI infrastructure were also under pressure as investors worried that Democratic victories could bring stricter oversight of data-center construction.

"We suspect there is going to be some scrutiny on this aggressive AI buildout," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank, told Reuters.

The selloff also spilled into cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin fell below $76,000, wiping out its post-election recovery as approximately $428 million in leveraged crypto long positions were liquidated within an hour, as Decrypt reported earlier today.

Stocks also faced pressure from persistent inflation concerns and uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's next interest-rate decision. Investors are awaiting Friday's October employment report, which could provide further clues about the direction of monetary policy.

Despite Thursday's sharp losses, the S&P 500 had not reached its first market-wide circuit breaker at the time of this report.

#5221. Robinhood Chain was built for tokenized stocks – But memecoins took over

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Gen Zs are rewriting the rules of wealth creation, increasingly trading the traditional financial playbook for a high-stakes game of chance.

From cryptocurrencies and memecoins to sports betting and prediction markets, the generation is exploring unconventional ways in pursuit of financial gains that once seemed possible only through years of saving and investing.

In this complex financial landscape, the line separating investing from gambling is blurring by the day. In fact, Ashley Embers recently highlighted how 37% of Gen Z respondents engage in sports betting, while 20% place bets online.

More concerningly, over half of Gen Z adults aged 18–29 reportedly redirected money originally intended for investments into sports betting over the past year, with 14% doing so several times a month.

This shift is also being reflected in a few corners of the crypto market, which is even better than memecoins.

One interesting example of this shift is Robinhood Chain.

When Robinhood introduced its Ethereum [ETH] Layer-2 network, the company planned to build a three-in-one infrastructure layer, which includes tokenized stocks, real-world assets [RWAs], and decentralized finance [DeFi] applications.

Expanding on this, Johann Kerbrat, SVP and General Manager of Crypto and International at Robinhood, said,

We’re bringing the best of traditional finance and DeFi together, and in doing so, expanding financial ownership to every corner of the globe.

The main goal of the team was to bring traditional financial markets on-chain to enable users to access tokenized versions of familiar assets through blockchain infrastructure.

However, the network’s early adoption took a complete U-turn from the initial goal. Rather than being primarily driven by tokenized equities and traditional financial products, Robinhood Chain attracted considerable attention from memecoin traders.

Expressing his opinion on the matter, Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev said,

If you hold a memecoin, you just get stock tokens airdropped to you.

This has raised an interesting question: Is Robinhood building the next generation of tokenized financial markets, or has it accidentally created another destination for speculative crypto trading?

Tokenized equities were expected to be one of the Robinhood’s defining use cases. However, the initial trading activity suggested that traders have found another reason to use the network.

Per Bitquery’s analysis of Robinhood Chain’s trading activity between the 16th and the 28th of July 2026, memecoins accounted for approximately 93.5% of trading across 63.5 million transactions. Tokenized equities, meanwhile, represented just 6.5%.

CoinGecko also highlighted this shift in trend. As per its July 2026 assessment, memecoins accounted for 79.2% of Robinhood Chain’s DEX volume, whereas RWAs made up just 9.69%.

These reveal a considerable gap between Robinhood’s intended use case and actual market demand.

Robinhood Chain has also enabled creators to pair their memecoins with tokenized versions of established companies.

This means that tokenized equities are not necessarily being used for traditional investment purposes. Instead, they have become the trading currency through which users speculate on unrelated digital assets.

Similarly, Bloomberg reported that daily trading volume in pairs combining Robinhood stock tokens with memecoins had reached approximately $443 million in early September.

Yet, despite the speculative nature of its activity, Robinhood Chain has recorded impressive growth since its launch. CoinGecko’s Q3 2026 Crypto Industry Report highlighted the network as the third-most-active blockchain within just three months of its public launch.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood Chain generated more than $88.9 billion in trading volume, averaging approximately 9.5 million transactions per day.

Daily trading volume on its native decentralized exchanges also increased from approximately $1.3 million on launch day to a peak of $3.5 billion on the 4th of September.

The company also added approximately $25 million worth of Bitcoin to its corporate balance sheet in October, describing the purchase as an asset-diversification strategy.

These developments indicate that Robinhood’s broader ambitions extend well beyond memecoins.

However, memecoin trading on the Robinhood Chain is not without its risks.

Bitquery’s investigation found that approximately 84% of the nearly 15,000 tokens launched daily never traded again after their initial transaction. The investigation also revealed that three out of every four open trading positions were underwater.

Meanwhile, Fortune subsequently reported that trading volume in these memecoin-stock pairs had fallen by approximately 96% from its early-September peak.

This highlights how quickly speculative enthusiasm disappears. Yet, despite these concerns, it would be premature to conclude that memecoin activity is sabotaging Robinhood’s broader ambitions.

In fact, the silver lining here might be that speculation could be serving as an unexpected entry point into tokenized finance.

Though the company may have succeeded in getting traders through the door, whether they stay for tokenized stocks and RWAs, rather than the next viral memecoin, remains the bigger question on the table.

#5220. Block Discloses Proposed $764M DOJ Payment in Anti-Money-Laundering Resolution

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Block, the payments company behind Cash App and Square, says it reached an agreement in principle with the US Department of Justice over an anti-money-laundering programme allegation. Its November 3 filing outlines approximately $964 million in gross monetary terms and a potential $764 million net payment after credits, but the resolution still requires a final agreement and court approval.

Crypto investors often think of compliance risk in terms of exchanges. A new filing from Block is a reminder that the same financial-crime obligations also shape mainstream payment apps that let customers use bitcoin alongside ordinary money transfers.

In its third-quarter Form 10-Q filed November 3, Block said it reached an agreement in principle during October with the US Department of Justice. The contemplated deferred prosecution agreement would address an allegation that the company failed to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering programme under the Bank Secrecy Act.

The filing describes a gross monetary component of roughly $964 million. Credits related to earlier regulatory resolutions would reduce the expected net payment to approximately $764 million, according to the company. Block says it accrued that latter amount as of September 30, 2026.

Under the contemplated arrangement, prosecutors would defer the relevant charge for three years. If the company fully complied with the obligations in a final agreement over that term, the DOJ would seek dismissal of the deferred charge.

None of this means the matter has already been settled in court. Block explicitly says the resolution is subject to a satisfactory final agreement and judicial approval. It also cautions that the company cannot guarantee the parties will reach final terms, and that losses could exceed what it has accrued.

That distinction matters in headlines. An agreement in principle is meaningful because it describes a possible route out of a substantial legal dispute. It is not the same as a completed final settlement or a judicial finding that every allegation has been resolved.

Block is best known for the Cash App and Square ecosystems. Cash App users can interact with bitcoin, but the company also provides payments, cards, lending and other financial tools. A breakdown in monitoring or due diligence controls can affect far more than a narrow crypto trading product.

The DOJ inquiry is connected to questions raised about the company’s compliance and risk practices following allegations aired in 2023. Block’s filing notes that a separate Securities and Exchange Commission investigation ended in March 2026 without a recommendation for enforcement action. The end of that separate inquiry should not be confused with the Justice Department’s proposed criminal resolution.

More broadly, investors have been considering the effect of tighter controls across crypto services. NewsBTC has covered stablecoin compliance restrictions affecting Coinbase customers, which addresses a different segment of the market but highlights why operational trust extends beyond fast transactions.

For a payments business, suspicious-activity monitoring, customer identification and escalation procedures must operate consistently at large scale. Even when individual transactions are small, the number of users and transfers can create a major supervisory challenge.

There is also an important distinction between financial penalties and technology investment. Paying a fine or reaching a deferred prosecution agreement does not by itself prove that controls have been fixed. Regulators and customers will look for the systems, staffing and governance needed to prevent a repeat.

The next step is whether Block and the DOJ complete a final agreement on the announced terms, including any independent monitoring or compliance obligations. Until then, the $764 million figure is the company’s expected net payment under a proposed resolution, not evidence that the case is fully closed.

#5218. Trump-Backed American Bitcoin Turns a Profit as Bitcoin Rise Lifts Books

Trump-Backed American Bitcoin Turns a Profit as Bitcoin Rise Lifts Books

American Bitcoin, the Trump-family-backed mining venture, swung to a roughly $126 million profit in the third quarter, a sharp reversal from the loss it posted three months earlier, as a jump in Bitcoin’s book value and disciplined accumulation powered its best showing yet.

The Nasdaq-listed company, which trades under the ticker ABTC and is majority-owned by miner Hut 8, reported net income of about $126 million for the quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with a $57.2 million net loss in the second quarter.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at roughly $221 million, versus a $45 million loss the prior quarter. Much of the swing came from a $197 million gain on its digital assets, as Bitcoin’s value rose during the period.

The company grew its Bitcoin reserve to about 8,427 BTC, up roughly 425 coins, or 5%, from the end of June, and lifted its “satoshis per share,” a measure of how much Bitcoin backs each share, by about 5%. Notably, it did so without buying any Bitcoin or issuing new shares through its at-the-market program during the quarter, relying instead on its own mining output.

“These are significant results, particularly in a challenging digital asset market,” said Eric Trump, the company’s co-founder and chief strategy officer, touting the profit and the growth in Bitcoin per share. CEO Mike Ho credited “a disciplined, Bitcoin-denominated operating business,” saying the firm continued “mining Bitcoin at a structural discount to spot.”

The mining operation itself had a tougher quarter. American Bitcoin mined about 891 BTC, down from 932 in the prior period, and its cost to mine rose to roughly $42,100 per Bitcoin from $36,500, which it attributed to higher seasonal power costs. Gross margin slipped to 41% from 49%. The company ended the quarter with a fleet of about 89,242 miners and 28.1 exahashes per second of capacity.

The results cap a volatile stretch for the venture. American Bitcoin notched a record mining quarter earlier this year as it crossed 8,000 BTC, but its stock has struggled, hitting new lows and prompting a 1-for-15 reverse stock split in July. Shares have fallen well below their debut price since the company went public through a merger with Gryphon Digital Mining.

The company’s profit, while striking, rests heavily on an accounting gain tied to Bitcoin’s price rather than core mining operations, meaning a downturn in Bitcoin could just as easily swing the figure back into the red.

#5216. Polymarket Expands Chainlink-Powered 15-Minute Markets to Gold and Silver

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Polymarket and Chainlink announced an expansion of their oracle partnership on October 29, bringing high-speed up/down prediction markets to gold and silver and extending the concept beyond crypto assets. The announcement says Chainlink has supported more than $11 billion in trading volume on the platform, but that figure is not a forecast of what the new contracts will attract.

Prediction markets need more than a collection of traders. They also need an agreed answer to the question being traded: what happened to the underlying price by the end of the contract? The shorter the contract, the more carefully that answer needs to be defined.

That is the backdrop to a Chainlink announcement on October 29. It says Polymarket is deepening its use of Chainlink as an official oracle for rapid up/down markets, including new exposure to gold and silver. The companies describe an expansion of 15-minute formats into commodities, equities and foreign-exchange markets.

An up/down contract asks whether a reference price ends above or below a specified level at a particular time. That sounds straightforward, but two market-data sources can disagree briefly, especially when instruments trade around the clock or a contract ends during a volatile period.

The oracle determines which information enters the settlement process. For a high-frequency market, the timing convention, reference venue, publication frequency and dispute-handling rules can be as important as the price direction itself.

Chainlink says its infrastructure has already supported more than $11 billion in Polymarket trading volume. That is presented as activity processed through the partnership to date, not the size of the new gold and silver market or evidence of profit generated by participants.

For traders, a well-designed oracle should reduce ambiguity about the outcome. It cannot remove all market risk, guarantee execution at a desired price or ensure every contract is suitable for every jurisdiction. Prediction market access and the legality of particular contracts also vary across regions.

Moving from cryptocurrency prices to precious metals introduces differences in trading hours, underlying reference instruments and price discovery. Spot metals, futures and other benchmarks can move together without matching tick for tick. A contract’s methodology must therefore explain which index or feed is authoritative.

The same challenge becomes more complicated with foreign exchange and equities. Equities may not trade continuously in the same way as crypto, while different FX reference points could apply across market sessions. Speed alone is not a substitute for clearly documented market rules.

The announcement is also notable because it shows crypto infrastructure being repurposed for financial questions outside the digital-asset market. NewsBTC has covered planned infrastructure for tokenized securities, a separate example of blockchain providers competing on market infrastructure rather than token speculation alone.

The next useful figures would be contract-level trading volume, order-book depth, dispute frequency and the ability of markets to settle accurately during difficult price moves. These operational measures are more informative than the existence of a new trading pair.

There are also consumer-protection questions. Fifteen-minute contracts can encourage frequent decisions, and transaction costs or spreads can materially affect outcomes. They should not be presented as straightforward substitutes for holding gold, silver or an exchange-traded investment.

Polymarket and Chainlink have announced an extension of their data partnership into new underlying markets. The significance will depend on whether the contracts attract sustained use and whether the oracle and settlement rules perform reliably when prices move quickly.

Zcash has set a new high in its network hashrate just days after the NU7 upgrade, which slashed block times by a third to 25 seconds. Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on November 6, 2026, at block 3,543,405.

Zcash network hashrate: 32.62 GSol/s, up 5.8% in 30 days. ⛏️ An all-time high. https://t.co/1vNROBAvd2

Zcash hashrate refers to the total computing power of all miners on the ZEC network. It is calculated by the current network difficulty, the average block find time set by the cryptocurrency network and/or the effective block find time of the latest blocks.

ZEC got 3x faster following the NU7 upgrade, which launched on November 6, with block times down from 75 to 25 seconds, and the Sprout pool retired, marking a new era for Zcash.

Faster blocks mean more room for shielded transactions. NU7 adds per-block limits: 330 Orchard or Ironwood actions, 300 Sapling inputs and outputs, a shared budget of 330 across pools, and no new Sprout JoinSplits. These limits more than double Orchard protocol throughput while reducing the worst-case sync load a spammer can push onto light wallets by about 37%.

NU7 does not raise Zcash's fixed 21 million cap; halvings will now come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving. NU7 also starts allocating funds for future mining rewards. Some 60% of aggregate transaction fees will flow into a public reserve that pays later mining rewards.

In what comes next after the NU7 upgrade, Zcash developers have proposed cutting block times in a potential NU7.1 upgrade just days after NU7 went live. The proposal would reduce target block times from 25 to 20 seconds, aiming to speed up transaction confirmations and improve user experience and network latency.

#5212. OpenAI Found 948 Linux Security Flaws—And Figured Out How to Exploit Them

OpenAI Found 948 Linux Security Flaws—And Figured Out How to Exploit Them

OpenAI says its autonomous security agents discovered 948 distinct vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, developed working exploits and drafted fixes for review—all for roughly $1.2 million in API credits.

“We chose Linux to study how effectively frontier models could find vulnerabilities and demonstrate their security impact in a codebase of this scale and importance,” OpenAI said in results published Wednesday.

The Linux kernel powers cloud servers, Android devices and much of the world's critical computing infrastructure. The flaws identified in OpenAI's experiment were local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities: An attacker would first need limited access to a vulnerable machine, but could then potentially obtain root privileges and take full control.

OpenAI's agents scanned about 2.8 million lines of kernel code, or roughly 7% of the project. “Our prototype identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits that could allow an unprivileged local user to gain root access” OpenAI said.

After grouping exploits by their underlying cause and proposed fix, researchers counted 948 distinct flaws.

The October run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, equivalent to around $1,279 per vulnerability. OpenAI compared that with historical $20,000-to-$70,000 payouts for Linux privilege-escalation exploits at hacking competitions, suggesting a hypothetical value of $18.9 million to $66.3 million if the same results were found manually.

An earlier GPT-5.6 Sol campaign found 166 unique privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in July for $513,690. A newer, unreleased cyber model found more than five times as many in October, even after the kernel had undergone months of fixes.

OpenAI also said its agents used at least 10 exploitation techniques unfamiliar to the researchers and outside experts they consulted—not merely existing tricks retrieved from training data.

AI companies finding critical bugs are just another proof of how systems are capable of performing advanced cybersecurity research achieving results that previously required significant human expertise.

Last week, Anthropic disclosed that an unreleased version of Claude had discovered and exploited serious vulnerabilities in widely used software, including Chrome and Linux. Some of those exploits could execute malicious code remotely with little or no user interaction.

The economics of this research were already changing before OpenAI's announcement.

Researchers at Vidoc Security reproduced several vulnerability discoveries associated with Anthropic's powerful Mythos AI using publicly accessible models for less than $30 per file.

Those tests showed that finding vulnerabilities was becoming increasingly accessible, although reproducing a flaw is different from developing a reliable exploit capable of compromising a protected system.

OpenAI's latest experiment goes further by automating much of that exploitation process, creating a potential advantage for defenders trying to patch software before criminals can take advantage of the same weaknesses.

The company warned that attackers with limited access to an outdated operating system may increasingly be able to escalate their privileges with AI assistance.

OpenAI is attempting to restrict access to its more capable cybersecurity models through verified security programs. Its Daybreak Red initiative provides approved defenders with access to specialized AI tools for vulnerability research, exploit testing, and mitigation development.

#5210. Best Crypto-Friendly Banks: 5 Options for Crypto Investors and Businesses

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto-Friendly Banks: 5 Options for Crypto Investors and Businesses

Which banks will support your crypto habits?

Finding a crypto-friendly bank in 2026 is not as simple as opening an account with a traditional financial institution. Some banks allow transfers to cryptocurrency exchanges like Coinbase, while others offer built-in crypto trading, digital asset custody, or specialized banking services for Web3 businesses.

The best option depends on where you live, whether you are an individual investor or a crypto business, and which digital asset services you need. Some providers also impose restrictions on specific exchanges, transaction limits, or crypto-related business activities.

In this guide, we compare crypto-friendly banks and fintech providers, examining their supported services, availability, fees, and limitations to help you find the right banking solution in 2026.

A crypto-friendly bank makes it easier for individuals and businesses to interact with the cryptocurrency market through traditional financial services. Depending on the provider, this may include allowing transfers to and from crypto exchanges, offering crypto trading or payment features, or providing banking services to eligible crypto companies.

Not all crypto-friendly providers offer the same features. Some let customers buy, sell, and hold digital assets directly, while others simply support transfers to selected platforms like Kraken or provide financial services to Web3 businesses. Some are licensed banks, while others are fintech companies that partner with banks to deliver their services.

Before exploring the best crypto-friendly banks, consider the main advantages and potential drawbacks.

If you’re looking for the best crypto-friendly bank to join in 2023, you’re in the right place! This list breaks down some of the top banks for cryptocurrency from a variety of fields, including traditional banking, business banking, and personal accounts.

Revolut remains one of the more accessible options for people who want to manage traditional money and cryptocurrency through a single financial app.

Revolut is a digital banking platform that combines traditional financial services with cryptocurrency features. In supported markets, customers can use its app to buy, sell, hold, and transfer cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ethereum. Available assets and features depend on the customer’s country and account eligibility.

Revolut also supports crypto withdrawals and deposits through selected external wallets and blockchain networks. However, transaction fees, supported assets, and withdrawal limits vary. Its cryptocurrency services are provided by separate legal entities from its banking services, and crypto holdings are not covered by standard bank deposit protection.

Wirex flips the script amongst the other ‘best crypto-friendly banks’ contenders. While other platforms began their story as traditional banks and slowly moved to cryptocurrency acceptance, Wirex set out to be the world’s leading crypto bank from day one.

Wirex is a global fintech platform combining traditional currencies, cryptocurrency services, and payment cards. Users in eligible markets can buy, sell, exchange, and hold supported digital assets, as well as use available payment services to spend their funds.

Wirex also hosts a cross-chain bridge, offers crypto-linked cards, and a Cryptoback rewards programme, which advertises rewards of up to 8% on eligible purchases.

Actual rewards depend on the card programme, subscription, and applicable conditions. Wirex is not a traditional bank; its services are provided through regulated entities and financial partners, depending on the customer’s location.

Mercury is a US-based financial technology company providing business banking services through partner banks. It is particularly relevant to eligible cryptocurrency and Web3 startups, DAOs, and investment funds that need traditional financial infrastructure to manage their operations.

Businesses can use Mercury to manage fiat deposits, payments, expenses, and transfers to supported cryptocurrency exchanges, including Coinbase and Gemini. However, Mercury does not hold cryptocurrencies or provide crypto trading services.

It supports most eligible US-registered businesses, including those founded by international entrepreneurs, but does not accept applications from crypto exchanges or money services businesses.

Monzo is a UK-based digital bank that allows customers to use their accounts with selected cryptocurrency exchanges.

Although it does not offer native cryptocurrency trading, customers can transfer money to supported platforms, including Coinbase, making it an option for investors who want to manage traditional banking and crypto purchases separately.

Monzo applies transaction monitoring and restrictions to cryptocurrency-related payments. For example, it currently blocks payments to Binance while allowing transfers to a range of other exchanges. Its cryptocurrency payment allowance is also limited, so customers should check the latest terms before making large transactions.

Ally Bank is a US-based digital bank offering traditional banking products, including checking accounts, savings accounts, and investment services. Unlike specialist crypto-friendly financial platforms, Ally does not provide direct cryptocurrency trading or cryptocurrency custody through its banking services.

Customers cannot transfer cryptocurrencies directly to Ally accounts, which accept transactions in US dollars. Ally Invest also does not currently support direct cryptocurrency trading, although customers can access certain crypto-related investment products, including cryptocurrency funds and publicly traded companies involved in the industry.

Ally is therefore better suited to customers looking for conventional banking and investment services rather than direct access to cryptocurrency exchanges or digital assets.

Choosing a crypto-friendly bank involves more than finding a financial institution that allows cryptocurrency transactions. The right option depends on your location, investment activities, and whether you need basic exchange transfers or more advanced crypto-related services.

Here are five important factors to consider:

Check whether the bank supports transfers to your preferred cryptocurrency exchanges, such as Coinbase, Kraken, or Binance. Some financial institutions restrict payments to specific platforms or apply additional security checks to crypto-related transactions.

Compare account maintenance fees, international transfer costs, currency conversion charges, and any limits on cryptocurrency-related payments. Some providers also charge separate fees for buying, selling, or withdrawing digital assets.

Look for providers with appropriate regulatory authorisation and transparent security policies. Check whether eligible fiat deposits are covered by a recognised deposit guarantee scheme and understand that cryptocurrency holdings generally receive different protections.

Crypto-related banking services are not available everywhere. Before opening an account, check whether the provider accepts customers in your country and whether its cryptocurrency features are accessible in your region.

If you operate a Web3 startup, blockchain company, or cryptocurrency-related business, check the provider’s business eligibility requirements. Some platforms, including Mercury, support eligible technology and Web3 companies but exclude certain activities, such as operating a cryptocurrency exchange or money services business.

Crypto-friendly banks and financial platforms make it easier to manage traditional money and cryptocurrency in one place. However, their safety depends on regulation, banking partnerships, and security measures.

An important distinction is that eligible fiat deposits may be protected by deposit guarantee schemes, while cryptocurrencies generally are not. Crypto assets also carry risks such as market volatility, custody issues, and potential losses.

Not every crypto-friendly platform is a licensed bank. Providers such as Wirex and Mercury may operate through regulated entities or partner banks. Before choosing one, check its licences, account terms, and what protections actually apply to your funds.

Several financial institutions and fintech platforms support cryptocurrency-related transactions. Revolut and Wirex offer crypto services in eligible markets, while Monzo supports transfers to selected cryptocurrency exchanges. Mercury provides banking services to eligible Web3 businesses, whereas Ally Bank primarily offers traditional banking and investment products.

The best option depends on your needs. Revolut is suitable for individuals seeking integrated crypto services, Wirex focuses on cryptocurrency payments and spending, and Mercury caters to eligible Web3 businesses. Monzo can be useful for UK customers transferring money to supported exchanges.

Yes, many banks and financial platforms allow transfers to Coinbase, although availability depends on the customer’s location, payment method, and account restrictions. Always check your bank’s current cryptocurrency payment policy and Coinbase’s supported funding methods before initiating a transfer.

Yes. Banks can restrict or decline cryptocurrency-related payments for security, fraud prevention, regulatory compliance, or internal risk-management reasons. Some institutions also block transactions involving specific exchanges. Customers should review their provider’s terms and conditions before making crypto-related transfers.

Eligible deposits held with licensed banks may be covered by national deposit protection schemes, depending on the institution, account type, and applicable limits. However, cryptocurrency holdings are generally not covered by traditional bank deposit insurance. Fintech platforms may also use partner banks, so customers should identify the institution actually holding their deposits and verify the applicable protection.

#5209. Ethereum (ETH) Gas Estimates Are Broken: Explaining the Fix and the Issue

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum transactions can appear successful, but there might be a problem hiding behind the scenes.

A Geth developer has proposed a fix to the client's gas estimation, according to draft pull request #36084 on GitHub. The patch addresses an issue in the current estimator, which could result in incorrect gas limits due to failed internal calls (calls from one smart contract to another) being ignored.

Although the transaction could still be completed, there is no evidence that the action the user wanted has actually happened.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a smart contract calls another smart contract, catches an error, and then proceeds to a refund, records the failure, or skips an item entirely. Technically, the transaction was successful, but the outcome is different for the user.

This could potentially result in wallets suggesting a gas limit that is enough to finish the transaction, but not enough to complete the work inside it. The developer also noted that EIP-8037 could make this behavior more common, since gas returned from failed internal execution can help fund the fallback.

According to the pull request, the change includes a stricter definition of success for gas estimates. This version of Geth would improve the way it deals with internal failures, counting failed internal calls and contract creations instead of checking only whether the transaction completes.

Even if the transaction completes, the estimate would get rejected if it produces more internal failures than a reference execution with a higher gas limit.

Nonetheless, the developer stressed that an internal call that always fails should not push the estimate higher indefinitely. The reference execution enables the estimator to keep existing failures without allowing additional ones caused by insufficient gas. The proposal also introduces a separate Amsterdam reference, preventing unnecessary increases made purely to access the state gas reservoir.

The developer states that they've replayed 432 mainnet transactions with the new set of rules from the Amsterdam update and that the suggested change fixed 64 out of 67 cases.

The gas limit increased by 4%. 254 additional estimates were unaffected due to the lack of the problem, with 3 cases being undetected.

For regular investors, the proposed change should improve the reliability of wallet estimates and reduce transactions that complete without delivering the intended result, despite introducing higher gas limits in some cases. Luckily, there is no proven link between higher gas limits and higher fees.

#5208. XRP could double while this yield strategy leaves you far behind

In a modeled doubling of XRP, a $10,000 XRP–RLUSD pool position reaches about $14,142 versus $20,000 from simply holding XRP, before fees and costs.

The XRP Ledger pool pairing XRP with Ripple’s dollar stablecoin, RLUSD, quotes about 4.7% annualized trading-fee yield. Joining this native pool changes what an XRP holder owns. The position becomes a shifting mix of XRP and the dollar stablecoin, surrendering some exposure to a rebound while cushioning some of a decline.

The trade matters with XRP near $1.16, down 7.1% over seven days in CryptoSlate’s November 7 capture. A hypothetical $10,000 pool position would accrue about $9 in fees inside the liquidity position over one week at the displayed rate if prices stayed unchanged, before costs. That is the scale of income to compare with the portfolio’s changing exposure.

At 13:07 UTC on November 7, XRPL.to’s pool data displayed a 4.7% annualized seven-day fee estimate and 0.09% weekly yield. The identified pool held approximately 1.94 million XRP and 2.25 million RLUSD. Data by xrpl.to.

The specific pool is rhWTXC2m2gGGA9WozUaoMm6kLAVPb1tcS3; its RLUSD issuer is rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De, matching Ripple’s official address.

XRPL.to reported about 1.14 million XRP-equivalent of seven-day trading volume and 3,502 XRP-equivalent in estimated fees. Its API guide describes the annualized rate as recent trading fees relative to liquidity, scaled to a year. The quoted income varies with trading and does not lock in a year’s earnings.

Those figures are estimates, not a reconstruction of fees actually earned throughout the week. The displayed fee figure exactly matches seven-day volume multiplied by the current 0.308% trading fee, yet the response records a fee update on November 5, inside that week. Without the earlier rates and transaction-level fees, it does not establish realized income. XRPL also allows eligible auction-slot traders to pay discounted fees.

Under the XRPL’s constant-product mechanics, trading changes the XRP and RLUSD quantities represented by liquidity-provider tokens. Fees accumulate inside the pool and become part of the assets those LP tokens can redeem.

Two comparisons are therefore needed. Holding everything in XRP preserves full XRP price exposure. Leaving an initial 50/50 XRP–RLUSD allocation untouched starts with the same asset mix as the pool but avoids its automatic rebalancing.

Consider equal $10,000 starting investments. In a hypothetical model with RLUSD fixed at $1, no fees or costs, and the pool adjusting to XRP’s new relative price, a 20% XRP rise leaves the pool worth about $10,954. Untouched 50/50 holdings reach $11,000; an all-XRP holding reaches $12,000.

Most of the gap to all-XRP comes from choosing stablecoin exposure in the first place. The smaller gap to untouched 50/50 holdings isolates the rebalancing shortfall commonly called impermanent loss.

The downside comparison changes the conclusion. With XRP down 20%, the modeled pool is worth about $8,944, versus $9,000 for untouched 50/50 holdings and $8,000 for all-XRP. The pool still loses money, but retains more value than the fully exposed XRP position.

Larger moves widen the rebalancing gap. Doubling XRP leaves the modeled pool at $14,142 against $15,000 for untouched 50/50 and $20,000 for all-XRP. Halving XRP leaves $7,071, $7,500 and $5,000, respectively. These are scenarios, not forecasts or measured returns.

One week’s quoted 0.09% is about $9 on $10,000 at unchanged prices. If that percentage is instead applied as a hypothetical uplift to the pool’s value after a price move, it offsets the modeled shortfall against untouched 50/50 holdings only to roughly an 8.1% XRP fall or an 8.9% rise.

That calculation holds the fee uplift constant while changing XRP’s price. Actual fees depend on trading and the path taken. The range is neither a capital-loss buffer nor a break-even comparison with all-XRP.

RLUSD adds separate risks. Ripple’s terms permit blacklisting and freezing under legal or compliance conditions; assuming a $1 price does not remove issuer or redemption risk.

The pool commits native XRP as trading inventory. A provider’s actual return depends on how much XRP and RLUSD each LP token can redeem, and their combined value over a matched holding period. Comparing that return after costs with both holding benchmarks over the same period can show whether the fees compensated for the exposure surrendered.

#5207. Zcash Upgrade Could Lock $16 Million in Crypto Forever

Zcash Upgrade Could Lock $16 Million in Crypto Forever

At recent market prices, those holdings represent roughly $15 million to $16 million that could become effectively frozen when the network activates its NU7 upgrade.

“NU7 (block 3,543,405) makes v4 transactions invalid, so what remains in Sprout is unspendable: frozen, not burned,” Zecstats says in its information card for Sprout.

The upgrade is scheduled for block 3,543,405, expected Thursday evening in the United States. The exact deadline depends on how quickly the blockchain processes new blocks, rather than a predetermined clock time.

Unlike Bitcoin, where transactions are generally visible to anyone examining the blockchain, Zcash allows users to conceal transaction amounts and the addresses involved. It accomplishes this through technology called zero-knowledge proofs, which can verify that a transaction is valid without revealing its private details.

NU7 changes that by eliminating version-4 transactions, the only format capable of moving coins out of Sprout. According to the network's technical specification, transactions using that format will become invalid after activation.

The decision addresses a problem familiar to anyone maintaining old software: supporting obsolete technology creates additional complexity and potential security vulnerabilities.

Developers haven't technically destroyed the coins. They will continue counting toward Zcash's circulating issuance calculations, and a future network upgrade could theoretically restore access, but that is not guaranteed, and the team has not shown any interest in doing so.

In fact, the specification explicitly warns that spending those funds may never be re-enabled.

Legacy holders are the people most exposed to the change. Anyone whose ZEC remains in Sprout must move it through a compatible withdrawal mechanism before the upgrade activates, or risk losing access indefinitely.

Sprout addresses begin with "zc," which can help users recognize old wallet records. Regular ZEC holders using modern supported wallets do not need to migrate their coins out of Sprout, although keeping wallet software updated remains important.

The blockchain also cannot reveal who owns the remaining Sprout balance, meaning nobody knows how much belongs to active users and how much is already inaccessible because its owners lost their keys.

Meanwhile, NU7 brings a benefit for everyone else: Zcash's target block interval falls from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, meaning transactions should receive their first confirmation approximately three times faster, according to the Zcash Foundation.

For Sprout holders, however, the relevant number is block 3,543,405 which will happen later today. As of the time of publication, the latest available block is 3,543,027. Once the network reaches block 3,543,405, any remaining coins in the old pool will be frozen under the new rules.

A trader on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, whose wallet was previously linked to the exploit of SocialFi project UXLINK, has started closing $148 million in open positions after suffering heavy losses.

On November 9, the trader launched a 16-hour TWAP algorithm to sell off the positions. The algorithm is set to end by 06:00 GMT on November 10.

The address was previously considered the most profitable one on Hyperliquid. However, the recent market downturn changed that, and the trader is now facing a net loss of $3.3 million.

The trader's Ethereum long position includes 30,282 ETH worth around $55.46 million, with a liquidation price of $1,740.

The trader also holds a 550,000 SOL long with 10x leverage. The position will be fully liquidated if the price of Solana falls to $65.6.

The selling of these positions is already putting pressure on the prices of all three cryptocurrencies.

In September 2025, UXLINK, a crypto social network with Telegram integration, suffered a hacker attack.

The attackers exploited the project's multisig infrastructure, which allowed them to drain the project's treasury and mint new tokens.

The total damage from the exploit and the subsequent crash of the UXLINK token price was estimated at around $42 million.

In August 2026, an anonymous trader deposited $11.54 million USDC on Hyperliquid.

Since then, the trader has closed five profitable trades with a net gain of $5.71 million.

At the end of October, the trader was still holding $5.6 million in unrealized profit on the Ethereum position.

The recent market downturn erased that profit, and most of the trader's funds are now at risk of liquidation.

#5204. Polygon wants to move 70 million POL without the wallet holders’ signatures

The proposed fork would make ownership proofs, later deposits and exchange accounting central to returning stolen coins.

Polygon's proposed recovery of roughly 70 million POL would move coins out of five hack-linked wallets without their holders signing a transfer. The plan would change balances through the network's rules, putting the authority to return stolen funds in the hands of governance and validators.

The November 4 proposal targets five addresses it links to stolen funds from security incidents affecting prediction market Polymarket and exchange Binance. Its dated reference tables attribute about 24 million POL to four Polymarket-linked addresses and 47 million POL to one Binance-linked address. The actual recovery would use balances at activation, not these dated reference amounts.

As of November 9, the published proposal still leaves the recovery fork's name, client release and activation block undecided. The November 5 governance agenda lists the proposal for discussion without recording approval. The separate Bor v2.11.0 release implements Uburu's StateReceiver changes, rather than this proposed recovery.

Under the proposed design, the upgraded software would read each listed address's balance immediately before activation, set it to zero and credit the same amount to the designated recovery address. This would happen before transactions execute in the activation block. Total supply would stay the same, and earlier chain history would remain intact. The proposal says Bor engineering must still confirm the design.

A single protocol rule would move native POL from five listed accounts to two company-designated recovery addresses. Approval and recipient verification remain conditions.

The rule would read each listed account's full balance from F−1. The recovery credit has not executed.

Before ordinary transactions in F, the five source balances would be zero and the designated recipients credited by the same amounts.

The proposed recovery changes balances at one block, so custody records need a separate adjustment.

Governance approval, recipient-control checks and Bor engineering confirmation are required. The activation block and recovery release remain undecided as of November 8.

Schematic of the published proposed full-balance rule. Account markers show address counts, not relative POL amounts. The panel compares successive steps of the proposed activation sequence; it does not depict observed recovery.

Governance approval, recipient-control checks and Bor engineering confirmation are required. The activation block and recovery release remain undecided as of November 8.

That would place recovery authority in a combination of governance approval, the specified address list and the software rule validators adopt. The affected companies would designate the recipients. Polygon Labs would confirm the proposed proof of recipient control. The proposed sweep would not require a transaction signed by the source addresses.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Those are separate responsibilities. Tracing stolen coins to an address supports the case for including it; proving control of a recovery address checks where the coins would go. The proposal itself warns that misidentifying an attacker-controlled address could move a legitimate balance.

Its recipient-verification requirements call for proof of control, such as a signed message or small test transfer confirmed by Polygon Labs, plus written confirmation that the address belongs to the recipient. The proposal also excludes other tokens and a separate category of blocked addresses, limiting the proposed sweep to native POL at the five listed accounts.

The full-balance rule creates another ownership question: later deposits would move too. The proposal requires balances to be checked again before activation and any changes to be published.

Those checks would disclose which coins the sweep includes, but would not establish that every later deposit belonged to an incident victim.

For exchanges and custodians, the proposed movement would create a difference between the balance shown by an upgraded node and the balance reconstructed solely from ordinary transactions. The proposal explicitly flags this problem for explorers, indexers and accounting tools.

A reconciliation would therefore need to connect each affected source address, its balance before activation, the designated recipient and the corresponding credit at the activation block. For custodians, the rule implies a separate balance adjustment, since there would be no ordinary transfer transaction to match against it.

The planned checks address part of that burden: an Amoy rehearsal would test that supply stays constant and unrelated accounts remain unchanged, followed by a mainnet-fork replay. The proposal also calls for publishing the transaction-free balance change and a verification script after activation. Together, those records would let operators compare the implemented change with the approved scope.

Customer reimbursement is a separate process. In its October 30 postmortem, Polymarket said 95% of affected wallets had been refunded in full that afternoon and announced $4 million being returned, including $1 million for pause-related losses. Those refunds compensate traders; the proposed fork would return assets to company-designated recovery addresses.

The next recovery milestone would require a governance decision, a final software specification, verified recipients and an activation block.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares fell approximately 5.6 % in after-hours trading on Monday, November 9, after the company’s board announced an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted in a foreign intelligence operation involving China.

The investigation has raised questions about executive oversight and potential leadership uncertainty at the world’s leading AI chipmaker

Nvidia’s board announced the investigation on Sunday, following reports that its founder and CEO Huang had been targeted in a foreign intelligence effort.

A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.

The board emphasized that U.S. national and economic security remain priorities. However, it stated that it currently has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia’s confidential information was compromised.

Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating fully. The board also expressed confidence in his leadership team and promised further updates when appropriate.

The controversy follows a New York Times report published in October concerning Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that purchases AI chips from Nvidia.

According to the reporting, U.S. intelligence agencies believe Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security, the country’s principal intelligence agency.

U.S. authorities reportedly investigated allegations that she helped illegally divert advanced AI chips to China. The report also described a close relationship between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang.

The NYT also claimed U.S. intelligence agencies discovered last year that she illegally smuggled advanced AI chips into China while developing a “close relationship” with Huang.

Jensen Huang acknowledged in a November 8 message to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologized for hurting her and their children, though he did not name the woman involved. “There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he wrote.

Nvidia-linked perpetual futures on Hyperliquid and after-hours trading on the Blue Ocean system traded around $176.13 on Monday, approximately 5.6% below Friday’s Nasdaq closing price of $186.64.

Nvidia shares had gained 3.91% on Friday, November 6. The company’s market capitalization stood at approximately $4.5 trillion, with Apple ahead of Nvidia in market value, according to the supplied market data.

Gary Black, managing partner at The Future Fund, which holds NVDA as one of its largest long positions, expressed concerns about Huang’s ability to remain CEO.

Cardano (ADA) has entered epoch 666, yet another milestone for the blockchain, which has been live since its launch in September 2017.

The number has drawn attention for its connection to the biblical 666, but the development also points to the Cardano network's basic timekeeping and staking mechanism.

Popular Cardano blockchain explorer Cexplorer displays that epoch 666 started on Nov. 5, 2026, and is expected to end on Nov. 10, with 1 day and 10 hours left to close. The milestone marks another five-day cycle finished in Cardano's long-running proof-of-stake system.

Cardano divides its operation into epochs, which are five days long and consist of 432,000 one-second slots. The importance of epoch 666 is largely symbolic and not technical, as it does not coincide with any major protocol upgrades or hard forks. But the number 666 has merely provided an interesting talking point for the Cardano community.

In a separate milestone, the Cardano network has processed over 127,000,000 transactions on mainnet. According to Cexplorer data, Cardano has recorded a total of 127,203,164 transactions.

In upgrade news, DijkstraNet, the Dijkstra hard fork testnet, has been hard forked to protocol version 12 and is now available for testing and integration against the full Dijkstra feature set, with the exception of Linear Leios.

Node 11.2 was pre-released on October 28 and successfully used to transition DijkstraNet into the Dijkstra era, and DB Sync 13.8.0.0 was released for all networks.

In separate upgrade news, Midnight has completed its upgrade from Ledger 8 to Ledger 9, bringing new capabilities for developers alongside security, compatibility, and performance improvements across the network.

Ledger 9 introduces native support for widely used cryptographic standards including ECDSA and Keccak-256, expands wallet and custody compatibility, and enables contracts to interact directly with one another.

Keccak-256 is the standard algorithm that Ethereum uses to scramble data into fixed-length cryptographic fingerprints. ECDSA is the standard digital signature method that networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum use to prove ownership of a specific wallet address.

#5200. Mercado Bitcoin Said Its Hack Was Contained, But Blockchain Data Tells a Different Story

Mercado Bitcoin Said Its Hack Was Contained, But Blockchain Data Tells a Different Story

An attacker drained Mercado Bitcoin-linked deposit addresses nearly four hours after the Brazilian exchange said it had contained a security breach, new blockchain research shows.

Bitquery's analysis, updated Thursday, traces more than $48 million in stolen assets across 11 blockchains. Its findings challenge the exchange's claim that it stopped the attack quickly.

The Bitcoin exchange announced at 9:56 a.m. Brazil time on November 2 that it had quickly contained the incident. Bitquery says 36,042 Ethereum customer deposit addresses were emptied between 9:27 a.m. and 1:56 p.m. Brazil time.

Those addresses held roughly $266,000, a small fraction of the total theft. But the attacker could still move those funds after the exchange’s announcement.

A customer deposit address works much like a personal receiving account for cryptocurrency. The exchange later gathers those coins into a shared online wallet, called a hot wallet, to process everyday transactions. Moving funds from a deposit address requires its private key, the secret that authorizes transfers.

Bitquery says the withdrawals were authorized directly by the deposit addresses, suggesting the attacker had access to their private keys or to a system capable of signing transactions on their behalf.

“That needs a key for each address, or a way into the system that signs for them,” the researchers explained. They warned that exchanges typically generate deposit keys from a single master key, meaning the attacker may still be able to access other customer addresses.

The amount stolen is also disputed. Initial estimates put the amount above $40 million, while Mercado Bitcoin's updated FAQ now puts affected assets at about $36.3 million. Bitquery estimates that $48.6 million was stolen across 11 blockchains.

Mercado Bitcoin's public updates have not explained the gap between its containment claim and the later transfers. The company assured customers it would cover user losses with its own funds.

Bitquery warns customers against reusing old deposit addresses until the exchange confirms they are safe. Mercado Bitcoin's reopening plan begins November 9 with balance viewing only; deposits, withdrawals and trading have no restart date.

#5198. Why Wall Street can use Ethereum without betting on ETH

Buterin’s November 8 monetary case meets an established framework where eligible institutions can post dollar fund tokens as margin.

Wall Street can use tokenized assets without choosing ETH to back its trades. That distinction matters to Vitalik Buterin’s November 8 case for holding ETH: BlackRock’s dollar fund BUIDL lets eligible institutions post yield-bearing fund tokens as collateral instead.

Writing as @VitalikButerin, he argued that ETH’s monetary properties deserve more attention than valuation through fee burn. BUIDL’s established collateral framework with OKX and Standard Chartered describes a route for eligible clients to support trading with yield-bearing fund claims rather than ETH.

@VitalikButerin explicitly supported keeping EIP-1559 and its burn. His argument shifts the emphasis of ETH’s value proposition.

In a follow-up post, @VitalikButerin linked the usefulness of holding ETH to assets issued natively on Ethereum’s base layer. More assets could give holders more opportunities to convert between ETH and other instruments or use ETH as collateral.

The institutional comparison predates the November thread. In an April 28, 2026 announcement, Standard Chartered described a framework allowing OKX VIP and institutional clients to post BUIDL in off-exchange custody at the bank while trading on OKX Middle East.

OKX’s explanation also describes an on-exchange route: BUIDL can be deposited and used as yield-bearing margin. In both routes, the stated benefit is that dollar yield continues while the fund tokens support trading.

The underlying exposure is cash, U.S. Treasury bills and repurchase agreements. BlackRock’s March 2024 launch terms described BUIDL as seeking a stable $1 token value, with transfers between pre-approved investors.

These features differ from the decentralization-based case Buterin makes for ETH. BUIDL is a permissioned claim on a managed dollar fund, with custody and eligibility requirements. An institution choosing it as margin is choosing that exposure and infrastructure, rather than expressing a preference to hold ETH.

The custody roles also differ. The original fund launch named BNY Mellon custodian of underlying assets; the later framework places posted fund tokens with Standard Chartered. Those are separate layers of the arrangement.
