#5197. Keno RTP by Number of Picks: What Changes and What Doesn’t

Home » Crypto Market News » Keno RTP by Number of Picks: What Changes and What Doesn’t

This article explores how keno pick counts affect RTP, hit frequency, and volatility. Using probability calculations and simulated sessions, it shows why more numbers do not necessarily mean better returns, and how paytable structure determines your long-term expected payout.

Ask keno players which pick count “pays best” and you get strong opinions: one or two numbers for steady hits, ten for the big multipliers. Both camps are usually arguing about the wrong thing.

Return to player, or RTP, is the share of every dollar wagered that a game pays back over the long run. In keno, that figure is set by the paytable, and each pick count has its own paytable. So the honest answer to “which pick count has the best RTP” depends entirely on how those tables were built. On a modern crypto board, the answer is often “none of them,” and the more useful question becomes what the pick count does to everything else.

Below, the math runs on a 40-number board that draws 10, using openly published paytables plus a few hypothetical edits. Probabilities are exact; session figures come from 20,000 simulated runs.

Traditional casino keno uses an 80-number board with 20 numbers drawn. Each spot count gets its own paytable, and operators calibrate each one separately. Published estimates put the house edge in land-based keno somewhere between 20% and 40%, and it can shift by several points from one spot count to the next. That is why old guides compare 4-spot and 7-spot tickets so closely.

Online and crypto versions changed the design brief. Many operators now publish a single RTP for the whole game and then build every pick count’s paytable to land on that number. When that is the case, the pick count stops being a lever on expected return. A well-run bitcoin casino keno table that advertises 98% should return close to 98% whether you pick one number or ten. Rounding multipliers to one decimal means no table hits its target exactly.

Before any paytable comes into it, the board itself fixes the odds. With 40 numbers and 10 drawn, each number you pick has a 1 in 4 chance of landing. Your average number of hits is simply your pick count divided by four: 0.25 hits on one pick, 1.25 on five, 2.5 on ten.

The chance of catching at least one number climbs fast as you add picks:

The chance of hitting every number you picked collapses even faster. One pick is 1 in 4. Five picks is 1 in 2,611. Ten picks is 1 in 847,660,528. None of this says anything about RTP yet. RTP is the sum of probability times payout across every paytable row.

Here is what that sum gives for three paytables published on a live bitcoin keno page that states a 98% RTP:

The spread between them is 0.04 percentage points. Over $10,000 of total wagers, that is a difference of about four dollars in expected return. Pick count and risk setting do not move RTP here; the gap to 98% is rounding.

The same arithmetic tells you what a fair one-pick table would look like. One pick hits 25% of the time, so a 98% table has to pay 3.92x on a hit. If a one-pick ticket somewhere pays 3x instead, it returns 75%.

If RTP stays flat, pick count changes two things: how often you get paid and how hard the balance swings.

That last line is the surprise. Five picks on this table is almost nine times as swingy as ten picks on Low, even though both return the same 98 cents per dollar. More picks does not mean more volatility; the paytable’s shape decides it.

Breaking each table’s return down row by row shows where the money comes from.

On ten picks at Low risk, the 2-, 3- and 4-hit rows deliver about 90% of the entire return. The 1,000x prize for ten hits contributes roughly 0.0001 cents per dollar, close enough to zero that removing it would not change the RTP at the second decimal. Medium risk on ten picks moves the weight up a little: the 3- and 4-hit rows carry 74%, and the 5-hit row adds another 17%.

Five picks is different. The 2-hit row carries 42.5% of the return and the 3-hit row 34%, but the 300x prize for five hits carries 11.7% on its own, the same share as the 12x row below it. On a five-pick bitcoin keno game, the top prize is a real part of what you are being paid back. On ten picks, it is decoration.

Knowing which rows carry the return shows where a stingy operator could cut quietly. Two hypothetical edits:

On ten picks at Low risk, cutting the 2-hit payout from 1.1x to 1.0x would lower RTP by 3.1 percentage points, from about 98% to about 95%. Halving the 1,000x top prize to 500x would lower it by less than one ten-thousandth of a point. The jackpot is the row players look at, and the one that barely matters.

On five picks, the picture flips. Halving the 300x prize to 150x would cost 5.7 points of RTP, which is more than the 2.8 points lost by trimming the 2-hit row from 1.5x to 1.4x. So for high counts, check the small rows; for low and middle counts, check the top prize too.

Here is 500 rounds at $1, across 20,000 simulated sessions per table. Expected loss in every case is about $10.

Same RTP, very different evenings. Five picks on Low produces the worst typical session and the best lucky one, because so much of its return sits in a prize that turns up once every 2,611 rounds on average. Ten picks on Low is the slow grind. With crypto keno, where a round settles in seconds, 500 rounds can pass quickly, so choose the session shape you want before starting.

Check that your probabilities sum to 1 before trusting the answer. If totals across pick counts differ by more than a few tenths of a point, some counts are priced worse; avoid those.

On provably fair games, you can also verify each draw against the published seeds.

To see how the published paytables look in practice, you can try keno at Jacks Club and run the spreadsheet check against the tables shown on the game page. The numbers should agree to within rounding.

Keno is a game of chance, and no pick count changes the long-run edge. Play only with money you can afford to lose. 18+ only; check that online gambling is legal where you live.

#5195. DOJ Creates 'Super Intelligence' Task Force to Guard Against AI Abuse

DOJ Creates 'Super Intelligence' Task Force to Guard Against AI Abuse

The U.S. Department of Justice is setting up a task force dedicated to policing the misuse of advanced artificial intelligence, as Washington races to build enforcement muscle around a technology it increasingly frames in near-sci-fi terms.

Announced Thursday, the Super Intelligence Task Force, or DOJ-SITF, will be led by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss.

Its stated mission is to make sure American leadership in “super intelligence” isn’t compromised by bad actors, whether foreign governments and their proxies, transnational criminal organizations, or companies and individuals using AI to commit fraud or other crimes.

The department invoked President Donald Trump’s framing that “America stands at the forefront of a new technological revolution in intelligence.”

“SI development will continue to be powered by American innovators,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement, adding that the task force would work alongside SI Force Chair Jay Clayton to keep critical AI technologies from being “manipulated by bad actors at home or abroad.”

Blanche said the DOJ would keep “identifying and prosecuting individuals whose use of SI violates the law, including by maliciously targeting American taxpayers, critical U.S. infrastructure, or other aspects of our national security.”

Notably, the effort isn’t purely about catching criminals. Weiss said the department also has “a responsibility” to “harden regular reporting on SI risk and response, and ensure companies exercise vigorous internal controls so that SI technology behaves as intended,” signaling that the DOJ wants AI developers themselves to tighten safeguards against models going off the rails.

The term “super intelligence” typically refers to a hypothetical AI that surpasses human capability across the board, and the government’s embrace of the phrase marks an escalation in how officials talk about the technology. Former SEC chair Jay Clayton has been tied to a broader Trump administration push around super intelligence, and the SEC recently added “super intelligence” to its 2027 examination priorities.

The task force joins a widening federal scramble to get ahead of AI risk. Trump signed an executive order setting up a fight with states over AI regulation. Earlier this week, the U.S. banking regulator OCC issued its first AI framework as banks battle rogue agents reaching into customer accounts.

The DOJ did not specify a timeline or detail how the task force would coordinate with other agencies, saying only that its work would “promote innovation and prevent the misuse” of the technology.

The growth comes after a series of changes Telegram made to the TON network earlier this year under Durov's "Make TON Great Again" campaign.

The Telegram CEO described it as "the largest deployment of a non-custodial crypto wallet in history" and promised instant zero-fee transactions for more than 1 billion Telegram users.

According to TON developer Andrew Rogozov, the custodial Wallet in Telegram will stay separate from the new wallet. Now, onboarding happens natively within standard chat windows.

Still, while wallet creation metrics break records, liquidity inside the network is lagging behind with total value locked at $42.01 million, according to DefiLlama.

These hundreds of thousands of new addresses are mostly making microtransactions, such as buying Telegram Premium, paying for in-app ads, or settling small P2P transfers.

Besides, Telegram's validator weight is raising centralization concerns among industry critics. At the same time, the native wallet is still unavailable for US users.

At press time, Gram is trading at $1.05. The token is still more than 87% below its 2024 high of $8.25.

"The crypto revolution is going strong," Durov said.

#5193. 2026 XRP Rich-List Thresholds Fall Sharply From 2020

Home » Ripple (XRP) » 2026 XRP Rich-List Thresholds Fall Sharply From 2020

The accounts multiplied, adding lower-percentage cut-offs required to land in any fixed-percentage tier.

The amount of XRP tokens needed to rank in the upper tiers of the XRP rich-list has dropped significantly over the past six years.

A comparison of snapshots from July 2020 and early November 2026 shows lower entry points across major percentiles, even as the number of funded accounts has climbed past 8.3 million.

The most commonly cited threshold tells a clear story. In July 2020, an account needed roughly 80,033 XRP to enter the top 1%. By November 6, 2026, that figure had fallen to about 43,313 XRP.

Similar XRP rich-list declines appear at other levels: the top 0.01% entry dropped from around 24.2 million XRP to roughly 3.6 million, while the top 0.1% moved from about 750,000 XRP to nearly 271,000.

Lower tiers followed a very similar pattern. The top 0.5% requirement fell from approximately 150,000 XRP to 78,000, the top 5% from about 10,400 to 7,200, and the top 10% from roughly 3,000 XRP to just over 2,000.

🚨XRP RICH LIST JUST UPDATED!!! 🤑 TOP 4% = 10,000 XRP!🚨Top 1% = 43,301 XRPTop 4% = 10,003 XRPTop 10% = 2,056 XRP Are you $XRP Rich?👁🤑#XRP #Ripple #BTC #Altcoins #Crypto pic.twitter.com/RfIwFPsMOq

Recent live trackers place the top 1% cutoff in a similar range, confirming the broader downward shift as the account base expands.

The decline coincides with steady growth in funded accounts on the XRP Ledger. The network now exceeds 8.3 million accounts, a substantial increase from earlier years.

Adding large numbers of smaller accounts mathematically lowers the balance required to land in any fixed percentage tier, even if existing large holders do not sell.

Most accounts still hold relatively little; the median balance remains in the low tens of XRP, and a large majority sit well below 1,000 XRP.

This XRP rich-list expansion has increased the absolute number of accounts that qualify for higher percentiles. The top 1% now includes tens of thousands more addresses than it did a few years ago, simply because the total base is larger.

Raw account rankings do not map cleanly to individual holders. Many people maintain multiple wallets, and a single exchange address can represent thousands of customers. One observer noted holding roughly a dozen XRP wallets personally.

I have about 10 XRP wallets. Yep, many holders have many so yeah there is that.

Exchange and institutional addresses dominate the very top of the list, so concentration figures that treat every account as a separate person overstate how widely the supply is held by retail.

Ripple-linked accounts and major exchanges continue to control large portions of the supply, including substantial amounts held in escrow.

These structural features mean the falling percentile thresholds reflect both genuine growth in the number of accounts and the persistent weight of large custodial and institutional balances.

The lower entry points make certain ranking milestones more accessible in pure XRP terms than they were in 2020. At the same time, the data does not indicate that large holders have broadly distributed their tokens or that overall concentration at the top has disappeared.

The XRP rich-list comparison offers a clear view of how the XRP Ledger’s account base and balance distribution have changed over six years. It remains a snapshot of addresses, not a direct count of individual investors or a forecast of future price action.

#5192. Your crypto can survive a blockchain shutdown. Your way out might not

Lisk’s planned January claims and Recall Foundation’s contract instructions separate token ownership from access to assets and treasury proceeds.

Lisk’s LSK token is continuing after its chain’s shutdown, but holders who left assets on its former Ethereum layer 2 network have lost its usual exit interface. The project says its portal and bridge closed on Nov. 2 and points remaining users to a manual claims process planned for January 2027.

Recall Foundation, which is winding down, describes a different path for staked RECALL. Its disclosure schedules its app to become read only on Nov. 30 and documents contract withdrawals afterward.

A surviving token, access to deposited assets and a share of an organization’s treasury carry different dependencies. A token balance does not, by itself, answer who must act to release funds or which infrastructure must keep operating.

Lisk plans manual claims for remaining L2 assets. Recall Foundation documents holder-initiated contract withdrawals after its app transition.

A surviving token, recovery of a stake and a treasury distribution are separate questions.

January 2027 is a planned process-introduction month, with eligibility and mechanics unspecified. Recall's route is Foundation-documented, not independently verified execution; original lockups and existing cooldowns apply, and Base execution is required.

Qualitative process map of the current official notices; connectors show documented steps, not amounts, elapsed time or certainty of recovery. No arithmetic or hypothetical state is used.

January 2027 is a planned process-introduction month, with eligibility and mechanics unspecified. Recall's route is Foundation-documented, not independently verified execution; original lockups and existing cooldowns apply, and Base execution is required.

Lisk’s current claims FAQ says it plans to introduce manual claims in January and publish more details then. Eligibility, the steps holders must complete and the timing of any recovery remain unspecified; January is not a promised payment date.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The January proposal also concerns assets left on the later Lisk Chain. The FAQ separately says the legacy L1 claim window closed on May 21, 2026, and missed claims cannot be reimbursed. The January plan does not reopen those legacy claims.

Lisk itself continues as a business finance platform. It says LSK already held on Ethereum or exchanges was unaffected by the shutdown and its Ethereum contract remains unchanged. The location of a holding therefore matters even when the ticker is identical.

Its published guidance has changed. A September withdrawal notice used an Oct. 31 deadline and warned that no recovery process or claim window would follow shutdown. The current notice records the actual closure of user-facing services on Nov. 2 and offers the January plan. It describes the remaining chain infrastructure as being switched off afterward.

Before closure, Lisk’s instructions required stakers to unlock their positions, wait three days, unstake and then bridge to Ethereum. The instructions allowed approximately eight days for bridging, including a proof transaction and a final claim.

Founder Max Kordek’s strategy statement, labeled August and subsequently updated, describes the pivot to a business finance platform for accounts, payments and approvals. LSK continues as its loyalty token. The token FAQ says onchain governance ended with the DAO’s wind-down.

Principal and rewards also diverge. Lisk’s closure notice says about 5.2 million LSK in its rewards contract, including unassigned and earned but unclaimed rewards, will be burned after shutdown. It explicitly excludes LSK that users staked.

Recall Foundation’s Oct. 30 notice says its board acted independently of Recall Labs. The disclosure concerns the Foundation and its subsidiary Atlas Networks Limited.

Its instructions say holders initiate unstaking and withdrawal themselves, using the staking wallet and Base ETH for both transactions. Removing the cooldown for new requests from Oct. 30 does not shorten original lockups. Requests already in cooldown retain their original withdrawal dates.

The Foundation describes an exit that can outlast its app, while still requiring an operating Base network and successful contract transactions.

The Foundation excludes staked RECALL from its planned burn but promises no buyback, redemption or proportional treasury distribution. It assigns funds to creditors, wind-down costs and contingencies.

Earlier CryptoSlate reporting on Silicon showed that exit paths can differ by asset. Lisk and Recall make the dependency on the next actor especially clear: Lisk must still define its proposed process, while Recall’s published route requires holder action after applicable restrictions expire. Continued ownership alone completes neither exit.

#5191. OpenAI Promises to Foot AI’s Power Bill After Voter Revolt. Who Enforces It?

OpenAI Promises to Foot AI’s Power Bill After Voter Revolt. Who Enforces It?

OpenAI promised Thursday that neighbors of its future AI campuses won't foot the bill for their electricity needs, two days after voters dealt data center expansion a blow at the polls. It also pledged public energy and water figures and limits on secrecy agreements with officials.

Its National Community Compact covers future campuses (a fancy rebranding for the term AI data centers) OpenAI both owns and operates, according to the company’s announcement. A separate policy blueprint asks legislators and regulators to apply similar requirements across the industry.

“We will pay the full cost of powering our compute campuses and ensure local residents do not foot the bill for our energy needs,” OpenAI said in its “national community compact.”

It also promises financial assurances before costly grid upgrades, so other customers aren't left paying if projects shrink or fail. Each AI data center would get a water plan, annual progress reports and independent noise studies.

The national compact does not describe penalties for noncompliance, a dispute process or independent verification of electricity and water figures. Residents could read OpenAI’s disclosures, but the document does not explain how they could compel corrections or recover losses.

The ownership restriction matters, too. Partners including Oracle build and own much of the infrastructure reserved for OpenAI, Reuters reported. The company has not said its national compact automatically covers those partner-owned facilities.

The proposed blueprint goes further on electricity costs. “Policymakers should direct state public utility commissions to create large-load tariffs that require large electricity consumers to pay the incremental costs they create,” it says.

A large-load tariff is a special electricity rate for major users such as data centers. The blueprint also urges mandatory reporting, narrow limits on officials’ NDAs and provisions letting governments reclaim tax breaks when developers miss agreed commitments.

The announcement follows a bruising election for the industry. Voters backed restrictions on data centers in multiple states, while candidates pushing for tighter oversight won key races. The results basically send a message to OpenAI and the broader AI industry that communities want a bigger say in how these facilities are built and how their operations affect the people living nearby.

OpenAI says every future campus it owns and operates will receive its own local compact and an annual public progress report.

#5189. Nigeria sets new crypto licensing rules, bans algorithmic stablecoins

Nigeria has banned algorithmic stablecoins and introduced reserve requirements for issuers as it expands central bank oversight of crypto payment services.

Nigeria’s central bank has introduced new licensing and reserve requirements for cryptocurrency companies, tightening oversight of stablecoins and digital asset payment services in one of Africa’s largest crypto markets.

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) issued the Regulations for the Operations of Non-Security Virtual Assets on Thursday, establishing rules for stablecoin issuers, crypto payment providers, exchanges, custodians and other covered service providers.

The regulations took effect immediately, though existing operators have 180 days to apply for licenses or authorizations. The CBN said the framework aims to support responsible innovation while protecting consumers and financial stability.

The move follows President Bola Tinubu’s July executive order, which sought to coordinate crypto oversight among Nigerian authorities without changing their existing powers.

Under the new regulations, stablecoin issuers must fully back their tokens with reserve assets and maintain an additional buffer equal to at least 2% of their value. At least 40% of reserves must consist of cash or qualifying highly liquid assets.

The rules also set minimum paid-up capital of 10 billion naira ($7.4 million) for naira-backed issuers and 15 billion naira ($11.1 million) for foreign currency-backed stablecoin issuers.

Additionally, companies providing payment-related crypto services, including exchange and custody services, must maintain minimum paid-up capital of 1 billion naira ($742,000).

The regulations also prohibit stablecoins that rely primarily on algorithms rather than eligible reserves to maintain their value, along with tokens that lack enforceable redemption rights.

Nigeria has taken a restrictive approach to crypto trading, previously limiting banking access for exchanges and seeking to restrict peer-to-peer trading using local currency.

The country drew international attention in the crypto industry over its dispute with Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume.

Binance discontinued its Nigerian naira services in March 2024 amid government scrutiny of crypto trading and allegations of currency manipulation. Nigerian authorities also detained Binance executive Tigran Gambaryan for nearly eight months before dropping money laundering charges against him in October 2024.

More recently, Nigeria’s revenue agency introduced crypto tax collection rules for digital asset platforms and peer-to-peer marketplaces in August 2026.

The company announced the return of Reactor and its screening products at 18:50 UTC on Nov. 7, saying it was emailing customers instructions for reconnecting with enhanced security measures.

The snapshot below records the earlier Nov. 7 position before that restoration announcement, not the current status.

Reactor, Investigations API and Rapid Lookup remain under maintenance in the captured Nov. 7 status.

In its Nov. 6 restoration instructions, Chainalysis asked customers who had not already done so to submit trusted IP addresses for its allowlist through their account team or support contact.

Those instructions required users to reset passwords and rotate applicable API keys after access was granted and before registering transactions.

Chainalysis said it was validating enhanced security controls during the phased restoration. The later Nov. 7 announcement confirmed Reactor had returned alongside KYT and Address Screening.

The recovery follows disclosures that went beyond the initial identity-data exposure covered by CryptoSlate on Oct. 31. The original Oct. 30 notice listed accessed user IDs, names, email addresses and organization role labels.

In a Nov. 4 update at 11 p.m. EST, Chainalysis said it had discovered on Nov. 2 that names, usernames, password hashes and live login tokens for all users had been exposed to a malicious actor. Password hashes are encoded password records; live tokens can keep a user signed in. That disclosure does not establish that every account was accessed.

The company also said abnormal activity on Nov. 4 prompted it to take KYT, other address-screening products and the login page offline. It was notifying customers whose KYT accounts appeared to have been accessed without authorization.

In that Nov. 4 update, Chainalysis continued to say it had no evidence investigation data had been accessed or attribution data manipulated. Its investigation was ongoing.

#5187. Bitcoin Fixes This? Paraguay President Resigns After Bank Lockout Hits 60% of Country

Bitcoin Fixes This? Paraguay President Resigns After Bank Lockout Hits 60% of Country

Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday after the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank left roughly three million customers unable to access their accounts, turning a banking failure into a political emergency.

The announcement did not end the confrontation. Paraguay’s lower house voted 78-0 to impeach Peña minutes later, sending the charges to the Senate as Vice President Pedro Alliana prepared to take over, per AP.

The bank’s shutdown has also revived an argument familiar to Bitcoin holders: Money held by a financial intermediary is only as accessible as that institution allows. Self-custodied Bitcoin works differently, although it comes with risks of its own.

As the Bitcoin OGs would say, “Bitcoin fixes this.”

Paraguay’s central bank placed Ueno into resolution after regulators found its solvency ratio had fallen below half the legal minimum. The process, announced on November 3, followed accounting adjustments to the bank’s financial statements and left its app, cards, and transfers out of service.

Ueno claimed around 2.9 million customers, more than 60% of Paraguay’s adults. It also held roughly $800 million in public-sector deposits, including pension and health funds, according to AP, complicating an already painful freeze on ordinary savings and wages.

Peña previously held a stake in a company linked to Ueno’s owners, a relationship that fueled allegations of conflicts of interest. He has denied wrongdoing and said he sold his interest in March 2025, according to Reuters.

“My greatest wish is that the return of those funds be guaranteed, that the Deposit Guarantee Fund fulfill its purpose,” Peña said in his resignation address. The Deposit Guarantee Fund would be the equivalent of the FDIC in the United States.

Mensaje del Presidente de la República, Santiago Peña, al pueblo paraguayo. pic.twitter.com/RBz6IfFV9L

— Santiago Peña (@SantiPenap) November 5, 2026

Outside Congress, the anger was less diplomatic. “Santiago Peña and the Colorado Party have stolen all our savings,” protester Luis Pineda told AP. “We are fed up with 70 years of plunder.”

The central bank says Ueno’s failure is an isolated case, not evidence of a broader banking collapse. It has announced a deposit guarantee of up to 228.3 million guaraníes per depositor, roughly $36,000, with initial payments targeting eligible accounts holding no more than 10 million guaraníes.

Bitcoin was born during another banking crisis. Its first block, mined in January 2009, included a newspaper headline about a second bailout for British banks, a historical detail long cited by supporters who distrust reliance on financial intermediaries.

A Bitcoin holder who controls a wallet’s private keys can authorize transfers from the wallet without asking a third party, like a bank, to unlock an account. That is the principle behind the crypto saying “not your keys, not your coins,” and the distinction from leaving Bitcoin on an exchange that can itself freeze withdrawals.

But Bitcoin is not perfect. Self-custody has its own risks: Forget your keys or lose them and there is no way you can recover your funds, there is nobody who can assist you, and no law enforcement agency who can do anything for you.

Paraguay’s central bank said Thursday its first guarantee payments would go to depositors with up to 10 million guaraníes, no Ueno debts and an account at another financial institution.

#5186. What Democrats’ US midterm sweep means for the CLARITY Act

The CLARITY Act faces a new test as Democrats control Congress, raising questions over consumer protections, ethics and what the crypto industry may have to concede.

Crypto companies contributed $233 million to political committees during the 2026 US midterm cycle, according to Public Citizen’s analysis of federal filings.

Democrats won both chambers of Congress and will take control in January, giving them a chance to reshape the stalled CLARITY Act, a bill to set federal rules for crypto markets.

In Ohio, Democrat and longtime crypto skeptic Sherrod Brown defeated Republican Sen. Jon Husted despite crypto-backed political action committees spending $64 million to defeat him.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s most vocal critics in Washington and the most senior Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, is expected to chair the panel in the next Congress.

Stronger consumer protections, tougher scrutiny of political conflicts and a shift in regulatory power are all likely to be on the docket in the next round of negotiations.

But a Democratic majority doesn’t have to kill the prospect of crypto market structure legislation completely.

Democrat Congressman Shri Thanedar remains hopeful that the CLARITY Act can still pass, but says any legislation must include stronger ethics requirements. He tells Magazine:

Can the industry’s political influence still be converted into legislation, and what will it have to concede to get there?

The Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act in September, with disagreements over ethics provisions contributing to the impasse.

The crypto spent $233 million on the 2026 US midterm elections. Source: Public Citizen

Democrats are already reportedly discussing how to reshape the market structure debate, with House Democrats said to be considering expanding proposals from Representative Maxine Waters into a broader market structure bill.

Related: Trump’s memecoin ventures derailed CLARITY Act, Scaramucci says

That bill could include stronger consumer protections, a greater role for the Securities and Exchange Commission, and new ethics restrictions on public officials’ crypto activities.

That could finally mean separating the industry’s push for clearer rules from the controversies surrounding Trump’s personal crypto ventures.

Democrats have already signaled plans to investigate the Trump family’s business dealings and other corporate interests, with incoming House Oversight Committee Chair Robert Garcia planning to pursue inquiries into corporate corruption.

Hadley Stern, head of institutions at Silence Laboratories and founder of Fidelity Digital Assets, says Democrats are right to “go after” the second, and the industry should want them to; that’s “what’s poisoning the bipartisan deal,” he says.

“A sitting president’s family launching memecoins and a stablecoin is a real governance problem,” he tells Magazine. “If I’d done that at Fidelity, I’d have been walked out the same afternoon.”

He says 2026’s digital asset industry is very different from the last time Democrats “held the gavel,” pointing to its growth from “FTX and a bunch of tokens” in 2022 to a federal law for stablecoins, Treasuries and credit funds onchain and tokenized equities on the way:

The industry may also have to accept more demanding standards if it wants legislation that can survive changes in political control.

Paul Brody, founder and CEO of Nightfall Networks and former global blockchain lead at EY, expects banks “to come out winners,” as they will “push for crypto companies” to be held to the same exacting consumer protection and security standards.

Related: Crypto Biz: CLARITY Act setback puts Coinbase in the spotlight

He says the industry has opposed this, but tells Magazine that “a wise strategy” would be to “accept similar conditions,” given that blockchain-native ecosystems are still “vastly more flexible, programmable and efficient.”

Lindsay Fraser, chief policy officer at Blockchain Association, also argues consumer protection and innovation should not be treated as competing objectives.

“We can protect consumers while ensuring the law reflects how the technology actually works,” she says, adding the goal is “lasting policy that earns public trust, gives builders a future in this country, and strengthens American financial leadership.”

That doesn’t mean it’s all smooth sailing to a potential compromise.

Brody says there’s still the possibility of a presidential veto, and points out that crypto is likely to be a “low priority” compared to “investigations of corruption and battles over budgets and the war.”

The midterm results came as lawmakers were already grappling with the fallout from the Binance hack, the largest hack in crypto history, with over $6.3 billion stolen on Oct. 29, raising fresh concerns about exchange security and customer protections.

Thanedar says while the legislation “wouldn’t solve every potential problem,” it would provide “much-needed certainty” and “security guardrails,” and the hack provides a “clear example of the danger of not enacting appropriate legislation.”

Maylea Ma, deputy general counsel at 1inch, says rather than making a stronger case for passing the latest draft of CLARITY, the incident “highlights problems the legislation does not address.”

The hack involved a “centralized exchange’s hot wallet and signing failure,” Ma says, but the current draft “has no insurer, no loss payee, and no hot wallet cap that would have mitigated the loss for Binance or imposed security standards that would have prevented the hack.”

Amanda Fischer, policy director at Better Markets, said the episode highlighted how “unfit for purpose the crypto ecosystem is for mainstream finance,” and crypto exchanges should not act as custodians, since it creates a “honeypot risk.”

Binance hack shows how ‘unfit’ crypto is for mainstream finance. Source: Amanda Fischer

Ma says the incident is “likely to impact” the next vote on CLARITY and could make lawmakers less willing to pass legislation the industry wants, unless it comes with stronger consumer protections.

Crypto spent years convincing Washington it deserves a seat at the table; now it will need to agree on the obligations that come along with it.

Home » Partners Spotlight » Bet25.com Launches Zero Margin Sportsbook to Eliminate Hidden House Edges

Berlin, Germany, 9th November 2026, PlayNewswire

Every sports bettor deal with the same issue: traditional sportsbooks hide extra profit margins within their odds. Behind flashy ads and complicated bonuses, regular bookmakers quietly lower payouts. When building a parlay or combo bet, these hidden cuts stack up fast

Bet25 is changing this with the Zero Margin Sportsbook, setting the new rules of sports betting. Built on honesty, clear numbers, and fair pricing, Bet25 removes traditional bookmaker tricks, so the real payout is received.

The Problem: How Hidden Margins Hurt Winnings

In a standard sportsbook, the odds you see are not the true odds. The bookmaker trims 5% to 10% off the price of each game to guarantee their own cut before you even place a bet.

On a single match, this might look small. But on combo bets, it becomes a serious problem. Because combo odds multiply together, the hidden house cuts multiply too. Every leg you add gives you a payout that is much lower than the actual math says it should be.

The New Rules: No Hidden House Edge and Naturally Better Odds

The Bet25 Zero Margin Sportsbook is not a temporary promo or a short-lived boost. It is a completely different way to run a sportsbook:

A normal bookmaker takes a cut on pick 1, pick 2, pick 3, and so on. Bet25 charges one single 5% fee whether you pick one game or five.

The difference is easy to see on a multi-leg ticket. Take a simple 5-leg combo where each pick has true 50/50 probability. A regular bookmaker will usually offer around 1.87 on each outcome to keep their cut but zero margin sportsbook will price it by 2.0, again because of no hidden margin inside.

Same five picks. Same $100 bet. Exactly the same risk. But Bet25 pays out $755 more because no hidden cuts were multiplied along the way.

Don’t Just Take the Word for It: Just Compare

Almost every betting site claim to have “the best odds.” Bet25 doesn’t need hype or marketing talk. Instead, the advice is simple: just compare.

Open a betting site side by side with the Bet25 Zero Margin Sportsbook. Check any match, build a 3-leg or 4-leg combo on both, and look at the final payouts. You will see the difference right away. It is not marketing – it is pure math.

Turning a concept this disruptive into reality depended on having the right technological backbone. Bet25 teamed up with Vegangster as its primary platform partner, working side-by-side from initial ideation straight through to full deployment. Vegangster’s flexible, cutting-edge architecture gave the team the technical freedom to execute bold and complex features without friction. In an industry where legacy tech often limits innovation, having a responsive partner who can translate ambitious mechanics into reality has been essential to Bet25’s launch.

Sports betting should be about making smart picks and getting paid fairly when you are right. By creating the new rules of sports betting, removing the hidden house edge, and offering naturally better odds, Bet25 gives players a clear, honest alternative to old-school sportsbooks.

Morpho says PAXG-backed USDC loans are live, while customer eligibility, borrowing limits and liquidation thresholds still apply.

Paxos launched its gold-backed PAXG token on Base on Nov. 6, adding another network for tokenized gold as Coinbase now lists the asset as eligible collateral for borrowing the USDC stablecoin. The launch extends PAXG beyond Ethereum and Solana to the Coinbase-incubated layer-2 network.

Each full PAXG token represents one fine troy ounce of physical gold held in custody, according to Paxos's product site. Holders can own fractions of a token, giving them exposure to smaller quantities of gold.

Lending protocol Morpho said Coinbase users can now borrow against PAXG through a new market on Base without leaving the exchange’s app. That gives holders a route to raise stablecoin liquidity against their gold exposure rather than selling the token to obtain cash.

Paxos's announcement described Coinbase Borrow among integrations expected in the “weeks ahead,” subject to product availability, although Morpho's same-day announcement described borrowing as live.

PAXG is live on Base. Morpho reports in-app USDC borrowing, and Coinbase lists PAXG as collateral.

Coinbase says PAXG collateral prices update during gold-market hours, approximately 23 hours on weekdays.

Coinbase says PAXG collateral prices stop updating while gold markets are closed, including weekends.

Gold-backed tokens can secure a USDC loan, while valuation hours and loan conditions still govern the collateral.

Morpho describes borrowing as live; Paxos's November 6 note used forthcoming language. Customer eligibility, asset-specific limits and liquidation thresholds still apply. Pricing states describe Coinbase loan-health valuation, not all PAXG trading.

#5181. Claude Gets Personal Finance—Anthony Pompliano Accuses Anthropic of Copying His Startup

Claude Gets Personal Finance—Anthony Pompliano Accuses Anthropic of Copying His Startup

Anthropic launched a personal finance feature for Claude on Thursday, letting users connect bank accounts and ask the chatbot what they have spent, what bills are due, and how much money they have left.

The announcement came with an accusation from crypto investor Anthony Pompliano, who says Anthropic tried to get inside information from his competing startup, Silvia, months before the rollout.

Claude can then summarize spending, spot duplicate charges or unexpected fees, explain interest payments, and build charts or bill calendars. Anthropic's example shows a user asking where their money went this month, then following up to find out what remains before payday.

"Access is read-only, and Claude can't move, manage, or invest your money," Anthropic wrote on X. "Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations," the company added.

The assistant can see balances, credit limits, account names and types, the last four digits of account numbers, and up to 24 months of transactions from accounts users approve. According to Anthropic's documentation, conversations inside the Personal Finance hub are not used to train its models, but account balances may lag and AI-generated figures should be checked against bank records.

Also, how Anthropic tracks its users’ financial data and uses it beyond model training is not completely clear—and this is extremely valuable information for big data companies.

Pompliano, whose Silvia product bills itself as a personal AI chief financial officer, posted a lengthy complaint on X shortly after Claude's announcement. He alleged that Anthropic personnel began approaching Silvia engineers in April, supposedly because they were interested in the startup's growth and computing needs.

"Anthropic was fishing for details on how we built our product and why it was so popular," he wrote. Pompliano also described an alleged steak dinner involving Anthropic representatives, claiming someone told the Silvia team that the meal was on CEO Dario Amodei's tab.

His engineers declined to divulge sensitive information, he claimed, adding that someone at Anthropic warned his team about the upcoming launch days earlier.

"Today, Anthropic launched a Claude wrapper that is masquerading as a personal finance product," Pompliano wrote. He also claimed Silvia's computing costs are roughly 97% lower when using its own models and hardware instead of frontier AI models, which most likely mean they are using a local model, likely finetuned for the startup’s specific purpose.

That said, Anthropic was not the first general-purpose chatbot maker to move into personal finance, either. OpenAI launched similar bank connections for ChatGPT in May, also using Plaid for read-only access to financial information, and Agents like Hermes, Open Claw, or Grok Bot can also do pretty similar tasks given the proper skills, permissions, and instructions.

Anthropic says Personal Finance is a first step and is exploring partnerships with licensed professionals and regulated financial firms. For now, the beta is restricted to U.S. customers on three paid Claude plans.

Hedera Hashgraph’s (HBAR) price trades near $0.067 with a market capitalization around $3 billion and roughly 44.3 billion tokens in circulation out of a 50 billion supply.

A move to $3 would imply a valuation in the $133 – 150 billion range. That is aggressive, yet the case rests on capacity the network already demonstrates rather than planned upgrades.

Hedera has processed more than 20 million transactions in the recent month and recorded daily peaks above 800,000. Its governed throttle sits at 10,000 transactions per second for crypto transfers, with production bursts already surpassing that level.

Verra is integrating the Guardian platform for carbon markets, while BCarbon has already moved millions of issued credits on-chain, shortening digital MRV timelines that previously stretched up to two years. Avery Dennison’s atma.io has tracked tens of billions of products on Hedera.

HBAR remains roughly 88% below its 2021 all-time high near $0.57. Daily RSI has sat in the low-30s. From there, continued volume growth on the live use cases above would be required to treat $1 as an intermediate level and $3 as a cycle high rather than a stretch target.

The pieces for higher sustained volume already exist: digital carbon registries tied to major standards bodies, production supply-chain tracking at billions of units, institutional collateral workflows, and AI-agent payment primitives.

When the next liquidity wave arrives, networks that can absorb real volume without congestion or unpredictable fees are the ones positioned to re-rate. Hedera is one of the few that already shows that capacity in production.

The path from current HBAR price levels to $3 is volume plus narrative plus cycle conditions. It is not a single announcement. The infrastructure is running. The rest remains speculative.

#5178. Jito’s Solana data feed puts a price on seeing trades early

Solana traders can pay to see transactions earlier through BAM without gaining the right to change their order within a committed batch. The product turns information timing into a saleable service, even as its execution rules protect the sequence of an already scheduled batch.

Helius's current subscription terms and BAM's validator revenue rules show how that earlier view is priced and who earns from selling it.

A BAM preconfirmation appears only after the leader has accepted a scheduled batch and committed to executing it in order. Unscheduled pending transactions are excluded. The stream therefore reveals committed activity earlier than a shred-based feed, rather than opening a window to rearrange that same batch.

BAM announced the service on Sept. 9, 2026 through Helius and Triton. CryptoSlate's July 2025 BAM coverage concerned the proposed sequencing architecture; the commercial data stream adds a separate question about access.

Jito does not sell the stream directly. Its distributors handle pricing, billing and onboarding.

Helius currently offers preconfirmations on Developer, Business, Professional and Enterprise plans, excluding free accounts. For each subscription in a slot that delivers at least one message, the charge is the greater of 300 credits or 10 credits per delivered message. Zero-message slots and uncovered slots cost nothing.

That means 10 delivered messages cost 300 credits, while 100 cost 1,000 credits, according to its published table. Concurrent subscriptions are billed separately. These are credit charges, not a stated dollar price per trade, and Helius says pricing is subject to change.

Customers also need to distinguish the two signals Helius includes by default. Its own preconfirmations appear when the leader executes a transaction and include its local execution status. BAM's arrive earlier, when the leader commits to execution, and carry no execution status in Helius's stream. Both precede shreds, but they describe different stages.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

A fixed execution sequence can coexist with paid access to earlier information.

The ordering guarantee concerns the committed batch. Preconfirmations are not finality. Sequence spacing is not time. The split is a published allocation, not measured payouts, profits or losses. Helius's own execution-stage signal is outside this BAM-only path.

Schematic of BAM's documented commitment-before-execution signal and partner distribution. A, B and C illustrate a batch, not actual trades. Revenue strip widths use the published 30/35/35 allocation on a 100% basis; no measured latency or earnings are drawn.

The ordering guarantee concerns the committed batch. Preconfirmations are not finality. Sequence spacing is not time. The split is a published allocation, not measured payouts, profits or losses. Helius's own execution-stage signal is outside this BAM-only path.

The commercial arrangement reaches the supply side too. BAM's published split assigns 35% of preconfirmation revenue to BAM validators, 35% to the Jito DAO and 30% to distributors.

Under the current validator rules, AgaveBAM and FireBAM operators are automatically opted into streaming. They can forgo the revenue and opt out, but self-service controls are not available yet. Opting out currently requires a ticket through Jito Developers Discord.

The validator portion is shared through eligible leader slots rather than paid solely to whichever validator produced a particular stream. BAM describes payments over the month after distributors pay the DAO, using priority fees attached to market-tick transactions. Skipped or disconnected slots earn nothing.

This gives participation a revenue incentive alongside an execution obligation. BAM says its Verifier checks produced blocks against commitments and that a validator that deviates can be disconnected.

BAM's operating model therefore puts a price on earlier information while enforcing a committed execution sequence. Assessing access means watching distributor eligibility, usage charges and actual stream coverage alongside those ordering safeguards. A fixed place in a batch does not by itself give every trader an equally early view.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

#5175. Zcash's NU7 Upgrade Goes Live, Recycling 60% of Fees to Fund Future Block Rewards

Zcash's NU7 Upgrade Goes Live, Recycling 60% of Fees to Fund Future Block Rewards

"NU7 has successfully activated on mainnet. A new era of Zcash is here," the project's official account tweeted.

NU7 has successfully activated on mainnet. A new era of Zcash is here. $ZEC pic.twitter.com/rPaSFe9h7j

"This is a huge milestone for Shielded Labs," Jason McGee of Shielded Labs, the Zcash development organization behind the mechanism, tweeted ahead of the activation.

The NSM tackles a problem Zcash inherited from Bitcoin: whether, as block subsidies decline with each halving, transaction fees alone will be enough to pay miners to secure the network. Under the mechanism, 60% of transaction fees will be removed from circulation and gradually reissued through future block rewards, while preserving the 21 million ZEC supply cap. Reissuance will begin in 2031, with the recycled funds spread along a smooth curve on top of the existing halving schedule.

The NSM was Shielded Labs' first project and builds on an idea that developer Nate Wilcox proposed years ago, originally called the Zcash Posterity Fund, McGee said. A separate proposal under consideration would require Zcash Community Grants to contribute 50,000 ZEC from its treasury to the NSM.

— Jason McGee 🛡 (@aquietinvestor) November 5, 2026

NU7 also limits how much private transaction activity can fit into each block, reducing the data wallets must scan to find their payments, according to the upgrade specification.

Shielded Labs' original design would have replaced Zcash's halvings with a smooth issuance curve. Community panels supported that change, but coinholders did not, so an alternative design that kept the halvings was developed instead.

"We still think the original design was simpler and better, but we respect the process that led us here," McGee wrote. "It should be difficult to change the protocol, and the process should resist capture by any single organization, group, or influential individual."

The upgrade arrives as Zcash's community debates the future of Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) and its share of the Dev Fund, the slice of block rewards that pays for development.

The five organizations that coordinate Zcash's coinholder voting, Project Tachyon, Shielded Labs, Valar Group, the Zcash Foundation and ZODL, have set out an expedited timeline for proposals and polling, saying "tensions were high" and that a drawn-out debate risked "deepening divisions within the Zcash community."

Proposals are due by November 8, with polls for coinholders and community panels running from November 16 to November 30. If rough consensus emerges, the groups will support a further network upgrade, NU 7.1, to implement it.
